crops.name: Wheat
crops.nutrient_requirements: N: 120 kg/ha, P2O5: 60 kg/ha, K2O: 40 kg/ha
crops.description: High yielding irrigated bread wheat requiring balanced basal phosphorus for strong tillering.

crops.name: Rice / Paddy
crops.nutrient_requirements: N: 100 kg/ha, P2O5: 50 kg/ha, K2O: 50 kg/ha, Zn: 25 kg/ha
crops.description: Staple grain crop sensitive to nitrogen timing, zinc deficiency, and water management.

crops.name: Maize / Corn
crops.nutrient_requirements: N: 150 kg/ha, P2O5: 60 kg/ha, K2O: 60 kg/ha
crops.description: Heavy nutrient feeder with peak nitrogen demand during knee-high to tasseling stages.

crops.name: Cotton
crops.nutrient_requirements: N: 120 kg/ha, P2O5: 60 kg/ha, K2O: 60 kg/ha, Boron: 5 kg/ha
crops.description: Deep-rooted fiber crop requiring steady potassium during boll formation.

crops.name: Tomato
crops.nutrient_requirements: N: 120 kg/ha, P2O5: 100 kg/ha, K2O: 120 kg/ha, Ca & Mg
crops.description: High value vegetable crop vulnerable to calcium deficiency and potassium starvation.

crops.name: Potato
crops.nutrient_requirements: N: 150 kg/ha, P2O5: 100 kg/ha, K2O: 150 kg/ha
crops.description: Tuber crop with high potassium and phosphorus demand for optimal tuber bulking.

crops.name: Soybean
crops.nutrient_requirements: N: 30 kg/ha (Symbiotic), P2O5: 60 kg/ha, K2O: 40 kg/ha, S: 20 kg/ha
crops.description: Leguminous oilseed with nitrogen-fixing rhizobia; requires adequate phosphorus and sulfur.

crops.name: Sugarcane
crops.nutrient_requirements: N: 250 kg/ha, P2O5: 115 kg/ha, K2O: 115 kg/ha
crops.description: Perennial sucrose producer with substantial biomass production.

fertilizers.name: Neem Coated Urea
fertilizers.description: Slow-release granular nitrogen fertilizer with nitrification inhibitors to reduce volatilization and leaching.
fertilizers.application_method_default: Split top dressing into 2-3 equal doses

fertilizers.name: Di-Ammonium Phosphate (DAP)
fertilizers.description: Widely used basal fertilizer supplying concentrated phosphorus and starter nitrogen for early root architecture.
fertilizers.application_method_default: Basal band placement below seed level

fertilizers.name: Muriate of Potash (MOP)
fertilizers.description: Standard potassium fertilizer essential for water regulation, disease resistance, and carbohydrate translocation.
fertilizers.application_method_default: Basal application and top dress at flowering

fertilizers.name: NPK 10-26-26 Complex
fertilizers.description: Balanced multinutrient compound ideal for soil low in phosphorus and potassium without excessive nitrogen surge.

fertilizers.name: NPK 12-32-16 Complex
fertilizers.description: High-phosphate compound suited for soils requiring rapid root development and strong initial vegetative start.

fertilizers.name: Single Super Phosphate (SSP)
fertilizers.description: Excellent source of water-soluble phosphate, sulfur, and calcium particularly beneficial for oilseeds and legumes.

fertilizers.name: Well-Decomposed Farmyard Manure (FYM)
fertilizers.description: Traditional organic manure that improves soil structure, moisture-holding capacity, and microbial biodiversity.

fertilizers.name: Enriched Vermicompost
fertilizers.description: Biologically active organic compost enhancing soil cation exchange capacity (CEC) and micronutrient availability.
fertilizers.application_method_default: Applied near rhizosphere during field prep

fertilizers.name: Zinc Sulfate Heptahydrate
fertilizers.description: Essential micro-mineral fertilizer correcting zinc deficiency, khaira disease in paddy, and leaf chlorosis.
fertilizers.application_method_default: Soil basal broadcast or foliar spray at 0.5%

fertilizers.name: Bio-NPK Consortium / Liquid Biofertilizer
fertilizers.description: Microbial inoculant fixing atmospheric N, solubilizing fixed soil phosphorus, and mobilizing potassium.

fertilizer_recommendations.recommendation_text: Apply Di-Ammonium Phosphate (DAP) as a basal placement at sowing to address severe phosphorus deficiency. Supplement with split applications of Neem Coated Urea at crown root initiation and tillering. Incorporate well-decomposed Farmyard Manure to rebuild soil organic carbon.
fertilizer_recommendations.application_timing: Basal at sowing + Split top dressing at 21 and 45 days after sowing
fertilizer_recommendations.application_method: Band placement below seed row for DAP; broadcast followed by light irrigation for Urea
fertilizer_recommendations.soil_improvement_suggestions: Incorporate 4-5 tonnes/acre of well-decomposed Farmyard Manure (FYM) or 1.5 tonnes/acre of vermicompost during pre-sowing ploughing to elevate Organic Carbon above 0.65%. Apply 10 kg/acre Zinc Sulfate heptahydrate basally to overcome zinc chlorosis.
fertilizer_recommendations.warnings: Demo Rule / Simulated Recommendation: Avoid applying untreated urea onto alkaline soil surface without incorporating, as ammonia volatilization losses will occur. Do NOT mix DAP directly with Zinc Sulfate during application to prevent insoluble zinc phosphate formation.
fertilizer_recommendations.explanation: WHY: Phosphorus is LOW (14.5 kg/ha) and Nitrogen is LOW (215 kg/ha). Early phosphorus is non-negotiable for wheat root development and tillering. Soil pH of 7.6 requires careful placement to prevent phosphorus fixation. Optimal potassium (260 kg/ha) requires maintenance only.
fertilizer_recommendations.admin_comments: Approved for Farmer Harini. Emphasize split nitrogen application to prevent leaching losses in Sandy Clay Loam.

fertilizer_recommendations.recommendation_text: Apply Di-Ammonium Phosphate (DAP) as a concentrated basal starter to rectify severe phosphorus deficit, paired with split applications of Neem Coated Urea throughout vegetative tiller development.
fertilizer_recommendations.application_timing: Basal placement at sowing time, followed by top dress splits at active tillering / crown-root initiation.
fertilizer_recommendations.application_method: Band placement 4-5 cm below seed furrow for DAP; broadcast onto moist soil with light irrigation for urea splits.
fertilizer_recommendations.soil_improvement_suggestions: Incorporate 4-5 tonnes/acre of well-decomposed Farmyard Manure (FYM) or 1.5 tonnes/acre vermicompost 3 weeks prior to sowing to elevate soil organic carbon and nutrient exchange capacity. Soil reaction is alkaline. Incorporate agricultural gypsum or sulfur compost during field preparation to lower active alkalinity and unlock fixed phosphorus. Soil is zinc-deficient (0.45 ppm). Apply 10 kg/acre Zinc Sulfate (21% Zn) basally to prevent leaf bronzing and stunted growth.
fertilizer_recommendations.warnings: Demo Rule / Simulated Recommendation: Specific fertilizer rate requires validated local agronomic guidance. Avoid broadcasting untreated urea on moist alkaline soil without immediate incorporation, as severe ammonia volatilization losses will occur. Do NOT mix phosphate fertilizers (like DAP or SSP) directly with zinc sulfate in the same tank or applicator to prevent irreversible insoluble chemical precipitation. Never apply nitrogenous fertilizers immediately before heavy predicted rainfall to mitigate runoff risk into local water bodies.
